subject: On‑prem provisioning & warmup: circuit checks and smoke checklist
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Jenkins <pete.jenkins@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: On‑prem provisioning & warmup: circuit checks and smoke checklist

Hi Pete / ACME Ops team,

As discussed last week, we’re scheduled to go live with the private deployment in your us‑east region on Thursday (04/08). Before we flip traffic, we need a short verification pass to ensure networking and warmup steps are complete. I’ve attached a concise pre‑cut checklist and the smoke runbook we’ll execute during the bridge. Please can you confirm the items below by EOD today so we can finalize the bridge agenda?

Quick checklist (high level):
- BGP session established and routes accepted between ACME edge and Redwood transit (verify L3 adjacencies + AS path).
- Public NAT for egress from control plane subnets (CIDR + gateway confirmed).
- Internal ACLs permit control plane and worker heartbeats (ports 22000, 50051, 443).
- Storage NFS mount verification on the on‑prem prep nodes (mount point /mnt/model-cache).
- KV cache priming plan: seed keys and validate <100ms retrievals for representative prefixes.
- Canary traffic plan: 5% of production for first 30 minutes, automatic fallback to hosted API on error.
- Observability hooks: logging streams, token‑level sampling, and alert thresholds loaded to OpsGenie.

Attachments referenced: acme_precut_checklist.xlsx, onprem_smoke_runbook_v1.1.md

Ask: Please reply with: (1) confirmed/unconfirmed per checklist line, (2) NAT egress IPs (or gateway), and (3) whether you want Redwood to prime KV cache or if you’ll do the seed.

Thanks — I’ll compile responses and circulate the final bridge timeline.

— Lauren Bishop
Principal PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: Pete Jenkins <pete.jenkins@acmecorp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform Ops <ops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: On‑prem provisioning & warmup: circuit checks and smoke checklist

Lauren — thanks for the checklist, that’s helpful. Quick answers inline: 

- BGP: established; we’re seeing routes from Redwood ASN and prefixes are accepted.
- NAT egress: control plane egress will NAT through 34.201.11.78 (we’ll add a /32 SNAT mapping for the control subnet).
- ACLs: confirmed, ports allowed from Redwood control plane IPs.
- NFS: mounts in place on prep nodes, but there’s a flaky mount on node‑03 (ops is investigating).
- KV cache: ACME prefers Redwood to seed the KV cache to ensure keys are consistent with production prefixes.
- Canary: agreed on 5% for 30 minutes, with auto‑fallback.
- Observability: we have the log sink configured; need the token sampling rule you referenced so we can validate retention.

We’ll aim to have node‑03 mount fixed by 15:00 UTC. If it isn’t, we prefer to postpone the cutover window rather than proceed with a partial mount.

Pete
Senior Platform Engineer
ACME Infrastructure
pete.jenkins@acmecorp.com

Thanks Pete — appreciate the fast turnaround. A couple of clarifications from the engineering side:

- NAT detail: 34.201.11.78 is good. We’ll add that to the control‑plane egress allowlist and configure the bridge to expect that IP for health pings.
- Flaky NFS on node‑03: ops, can you share the mount error (dmesg/syslog) in the Drive link? If it’s a transient race, we can proceed with node‑03 excluded from the initial warmup; KV cache priming won’t require that node.
- Token sampling: Lauren, I’ll attach the sampling rule JSON and add it to the Drive folder. ACME — once you load it, please send a quick smoke event so we verify the pipeline.

Bridge logistics:
- Draft bridge start: 2027‑04‑08 14:00 UTC. Duration 60m for initial activation + 2h standby.
- Bridge room: https://meetings.example.com/rooms/redwood-cutover-bridge
- Runbook owner: Jonas Weber (we’ll call steps in order: network, control plane, storage, kv‑warm, canary).

I’ve attached the current network diagram that shows the transit CIDRs and the expected ACLs.

— Jonas
Engineering Lead, Deployments
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

We ran the storage health script and got green for all prep nodes. Token sampling rule loaded; sent a verification event and saw it in your logging stream (sample id s-7b2).

We consider the checklist items confirmed from ACME side. We’ll join the bridge at the scheduled time and run the smoke steps you provided. I’ve attached the signed go‑live acknowledgement for records.
